checks.label: Content-Security-Policy
checks.source: CSP Level 3, 'The Content-Security-Policy HTTP Response Header Field' and 'Policy lists'; OWASP Secure Headers Project
checks.applicability: Applies to every successfully fetched document response. Always applicable: the check judges the response itself (its transport or one of its headers), and every successfully fetched response has a scheme and a header set, so no page lies outside its scope.
checks.expectation:
Fails when the response carries no enforced Content-Security-Policy header. A Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only header does not enforce anything (CSP3, report-only header) and does not count. Field names are case-insensitive (RFC 9110 §5.1); several CSP headers form one policy list and count as present.

Always applicable: every document response is in scope. Known gap: a policy delivered by <meta http-equiv> (CSP3, 'The <meta> element') is enforced by browsers but not read by this header-only analyzer.

checks.label: Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy
checks.source: HTML Standard, 'Cross-origin opener policies'; auditmysite #578 header tiers
checks.applicability: Applies to every successfully fetched top-level document response. Always applicable: the check judges the response itself (its transport or one of its headers), and every successfully fetched response has a scheme and a header set, so no page lies outside its scope.
checks.expectation: Reports a review (needs_review), never a confirmed violation, when the response sets no Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: COOP is an opt-in isolation mechanism whose need depends on deployment context (SharedArrayBuffer, cross-origin popups) that a single fetch cannot observe, so the finding asks a human to verify. A present header passes.

checks.label: Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy
checks.source: Fetch Standard, 'Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy header'; auditmysite #578 header tiers
checks.applicability: Applies to every successfully fetched response. Always applicable: the check judges the response itself (its transport or one of its headers), and every successfully fetched response has a scheme and a header set, so no page lies outside its scope.
checks.expectation: Reports a review (needs_review), never a confirmed violation, when the response sets no Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: whether other origins may embed the resource is a deployment decision a single fetch cannot observe. A present header passes.

checks.label: Permissions-Policy
checks.source: Permissions Policy (W3C), 'The Permissions-Policy HTTP header field'; OWASP Secure Headers Project
checks.applicability: Applies to every successfully fetched document response. Always applicable: the check judges the response itself (its transport or one of its headers), and every successfully fetched response has a scheme and a header set, so no page lies outside its scope.
checks.expectation: Fails when the response has no Permissions-Policy header. A present but empty or all-wildcard header is Permissions-Policy:permissions_policy_permissive, not this id.

checks.label: Referrer-Policy
checks.source: Referrer Policy (W3C), 'Delivery via Referrer-Policy header'; OWASP Secure Headers Project
checks.applicability: Applies to every successfully fetched document response. Always applicable: the check judges the response itself (its transport or one of its headers), and every successfully fetched response has a scheme and a header set, so no page lies outside its scope.
checks.expectation: Fails when the response has no Referrer-Policy header. Field names are case-insensitive. Known gap: <meta name="referrer"> (HTML, 'Standard metadata names: referrer') also sets the policy and is not read by this header-only analyzer.

checks.label: Strict-Transport-Security
checks.source: RFC 6797 §6.1 (STS header), §7.2 and §8.1 (the header is only honoured over secure transport)
checks.applicability: Applies to documents served over HTTPS; over plain HTTP the header is ignored by user agents, so the check does not apply.
checks.expectation: Fails when an HTTPS response carries no Strict-Transport-Security header. Over plain HTTP the check does not apply (not_applicable), with or without the header. Field names are case-insensitive.

checks.label: X-Content-Type-Options
checks.source: Fetch Standard, 'X-Content-Type-Options header'; OWASP Secure Headers Project
checks.applicability: Applies to every successfully fetched document response. Always applicable: the check judges the response itself (its transport or one of its headers), and every successfully fetched response has a scheme and a header set, so no page lies outside its scope.
checks.expectation: Fails when the response has no X-Content-Type-Options header; nosniff is the only defined value. Field names are case-insensitive.

checks.label: X-Frame-Options
checks.source: HTML Standard, 'The X-Frame-Options header' (a CSP frame-ancestors directive takes precedence); RFC 7034; OWASP Clickjacking Defense Cheat Sheet
checks.applicability: Applies to document responses whose enforced CSP sets no frame-ancestors directive; with frame-ancestors, X-Frame-Options is not consulted at all.
checks.expectation: Fails when neither X-Frame-Options nor an enforced CSP frame-ancestors directive protects the document against framing. With frame-ancestors present the check does not apply (not_applicable), whether XFO is set or not; a report-only CSP's frame-ancestors does not count. XFO DENY/SAMEORIGIN passes.
